precepts.text: In as much as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me. When we biting and devouring each other, when you be angry with your brother without a cause, you slandering him: you're not slandering us, you slandering Christ, because Christ put us in this position.
precepts.point: When the chief priests and Pharisees had heard his parables, they perceived that he spake of them. So they knew: damn, this negro talking about us. Rightfully so. And they still wanted to lay hands on him, because the words was cut and deep, and they knew that Christ would take away their place.

note.label: The Inevitability of Obsolescence & Agony of Defeat

precepts.why:
In the parable the husbandmen, the Pharisees, beat the servants and killed the son. They knew who he was: “This is the heir; come, let us kill him.” To say that, they had to acknowledge the works of Christ and know this man is the Messiah, and they still rejected him.

Christ shows where that same hatred lands today: “Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.” If you do anything to one of these men, even give them a sip of water, you do it unto Christ.

Some of these black Hebrew Israelites right now may say, well, brother, we not talking about Yahawashi, we not talking about Christ; our anger is towards you, we slander you. No. When we are biting and devouring each other, when you are angry with your brother without a cause, when you slander and hate, you are not slandering us. You are slandering Christ, because Christ put us in this position.

The only difference is we can't do nothing about it. We are going to stay in the spirit and continue to do what God called us to do. Christ can do something about it. He can do a lot of things. That's why they call him the king of terrors, and the stone that falls on the wicked husbandmen “will grind him to powder.”

precepts.text: The parable of the talents: the man who hid his talent in the earth did nothing with the understanding God gave him, and his Lord called him a wicked and slothful servant, and said, take therefore the talent from him, and give it unto him which hath ten talents. A lot of you think your gift gives you job security; realize that when you do not utilize that gift, God will take it from you and put the spirit on somebody else to take this truth even further. If you cannot be used, you are useless; and none of you are useless, because we all have been called for a reason. There is something in you that you have to give to the nation.
precepts.point: Nobody should be bogging down your talents and gifts; we should be accentuating those gifts, furthering them, and teaching others those talents where possible.

note.label: Member's In The Body

precepts.why:
We have to utilize the gifts God gives us in this truth. A lot of you think your gift gives you job security. Realize that when you don't use it, God will take it from you and put the spirit on somebody else to take the truth even further. The parable of the talents shows it; the talent is money, standing for the understanding God bestows on you.

“Then he which had received the one talent came and said, Lord, I knew thee that thou art an hard man, reaping where thou hast not sown, and gathering where thou hast not strawed: And I was afraid, and went and hid thy talent in the earth”. He hid that understanding, that gift, and did nothing with it.

Watch what Christ says: “Thou wicked and slothful servant”. “Thou oughtest therefore to have put my money to the exchangers, and then at my coming I should have received mine own with usury.” Even if you couldn't do anything else, you could have put it with the exchangers so something could be reaped. “Take therefore the talent from him, and give it unto him which hath ten talents.”

We have seen it time and again: brothers and sisters with talents who hide them, or hold them over us: you can't do this without me. Know that yes, it can be done without you. If you can't be used, you are useless. But none of you are useless. We all have been called for a reason; there is something in you that you have to give to build the nation. The quicker we understand that, the quicker we get out of here.

note.label: Matthew 25: The Ten Virgins, the Talents, and the Sheep and the Goats

precepts.why:
The foolish virgins came afterward saying, “Lord, Lord, open to us”, and were answered, “Verily I say unto you, I know you not.” Christ had already said who gets in: “Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven.”

Saying Lord, Lord is not enough. The foolish took their lamps and took no oil with them, and the oil is the wisdom of the scriptures. Calling on his name while breaking the commandments is exactly this. Men bless what the law calls an abomination and still say Lord, Lord, and the door is shut on them.

The one who enters is the one who does the will of the Father. That is the difference between the wise and the foolish.

precepts.text: I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart. That is the will of the Father, and the foolish did not have it.
precepts.point: Calling on his name while breaking the commandments is exactly this. Men bless what the law calls an abomination and still say Lord, Lord.

note.label: Matthew 25: The Ten Virgins, the Talents, and the Sheep and the Goats

precepts.why:
What is the will of the Father that the foolish did not do? David says it: “I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.” The will of the Father is his law, kept in the heart.

That is the oil the wise took in their vessels with their lamps, the wisdom of the scriptures, and the foolish did not have it. When the cry came at midnight, the wise were ready and went in with the bridegroom, and the foolish were left outside saying Lord, Lord. Watch therefore: have the law within your heart, because no one knows the day nor the hour wherein the Son of man cometh.

note.label: The War Between Blacks & Whites

precepts.why:
“When the Son of man shall come in his glory, and all the holy angels with him”: that is the thousands of heaven the man waxed strong with. “Then shall he sit upon the throne of his glory: And before him shall be gathered all nations: and he shall separate them one from another, as a shepherd divideth his sheep from the goats”.

The sheep on his right hand hear, “Come, ye blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world”. He comes with the angels of heaven, and he separates.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Breakdown Of Revelation 16

precepts.why: “Watch therefore, for ye know neither the day nor the hour wherein the Son of man cometh.” Pay attention to what is happening in the world. Read the scriptures, then search the news, and go outside the New York Times, the Daily News and the American news media in general.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

precepts.why:
Who are the virgins? This is not talking about multiple wives for you thirsty brothers out there. “For as a young man marrieth a virgin, so shall thy sons marry thee”: marry the Lord. “And as the bridegroom rejoiceth over the bride, so shall thy God rejoice over thee.”

So the virgins are the nation of Israel, and the Lord Christ himself is the bridegroom. And in Psalms 19 the sun is the bridegroom, so the sun represents Christ.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

precepts.why: “There is treasure to be desired and oil in the dwelling of the wise.” The oil is understanding, in the dwelling of the wise: the understanding of the Bible. That is the oil the wise virgins carried in their vessels.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

precepts.why: Now the lamp: “For the commandment is a lamp; and the law is light.” The lamps are the commandments, and the oil is the understanding of them.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

precepts.why:
The cry made at midnight: “The voice of him that crieth in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make straight in the desert a highway for our God.” A voice that cries in the wilderness: a cry.

That voice is John the Baptist, who was Elijah. Before Christ came, John was the forerunner, preparing the way of the Lord.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

precepts.why:
“Behold, I will send my messenger, and he shall prepare the way before me: and the Lord, whom ye seek, shall suddenly come to his temple, even the messenger of the covenant, whom ye delight in: behold, he shall come, saith the Lord of hosts.”

This is the same messenger Isaiah prophesied of, John, Elijah, sent before Christ. And likewise, before Christ returns, he is sent again, to wake up those that sleep, that are in darkness, all over again. Here we are. That is the cry at midnight: Behold, the bridegroom cometh.

note.label: Escape New Years | Armageddon: Chain Of Events

precepts.why:
When the Lord was dealing with the two types of servants: “For I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink: I was a stranger, and ye took me in: Naked, and ye clothed me: I was sick, and ye visited me: I was in prison, and ye came unto me. Then shall the righteous answer him, saying, Lord, when saw we thee an hungred, and fed thee? or thirsty, and gave thee drink?”

These men were doing it naturally. They know when a brother is sick to go see him, when a brother is hungry to feed him, when a brother is naked to clothe him. The wicked seem confused, but to the righteous it’s a natural thing. You are going to know who you are by your works. “Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.”

You will know your role, your lot, what to do; you don’t need the Lord to guide you that way, because this is your job. That’s why he says, I will send you my servants Isaiah and Jeremiah: these men are going to set us in the right order we’re supposed to be in and tell us what to do. Brother, you need to visit brothers in jail, write these brothers in jail, be in their community and fix their community, be in the hospital visiting the brothers that get sick or get shot. That’s going to be natural to the righteous man; the simple man and the wicked man are not going to do none of that.

points: Christ was telling us to watch: always be aware, understand what is happening, what is going on in the world.
Mark 13:35 says it the same way: you know not when the master of the house cometh, at evening, at midnight, at the cockcrowing or in the morning, lest coming suddenly he find you sleeping.

Matthew 24:36 kills the trinity: of that day and hour knoweth no man, no not the angels of heaven, but the Father only. If they are co-eternal and co-existing and all the same, why does only the Father know when Christ returns?

note.label: Matthew 25:1-12 | Excerpt from 'The Negro Bible: The Making Of A Slave'

points: I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: charity. I'm reading this because when you're visiting them, bringing them gifts, praying for them, anointing them, remember you're not just doing it to them. Yes, that's your brother, that's your sister. But who is the father of us? The Lord feels these things. When that brother perks up, when that sister perks up, the Lord feels it, just like a good father.

note.label: Visiting The Sick

points: Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me: whatever you do to your brother, you do it to Christ. These Christians say, I've got a personal relationship. No, this is how you get a personal relationship with Christ: you do it to your brother.

That's how I know you don't give a damn about the sick, because Christ says, when you've done it to the least of these my brethren, you have done it unto me, and it's in red. Christians are the farthest thing from what God wants in his kingdom, because everything he says, you do the opposite.

note.label: Visiting The Sick

points: When the Son of man shall come in his glory: the second coming of Christ, in his glory and all power.

note.label: Life Eternal Or Everlasting Punishment

points: He shall separate them one from another, as a shepherd divideth his sheep from the goats: he's talking about the righteous of the children of Israel and the wicked of the children of Israel. To extend it even further, the sheep would be the children of Israel and the goats the other nations. But specifically: the sheep, the righteous, and the goats, the wicked of our people.
Anybody know anything about farming, sheep are very docile. They're not aggressive. They don't fight back, and they follow their shepherd.

note.label: Life Eternal Or Everlasting Punishment

points: You got many people today of the children of Israel that don't want to hear nothing about these scriptures. They want to do their own thing. They worship their own God according to the figment of their imagination. So we go out and teach, but in the end days when Christ come on the scene, he's going to completely separate all the wicked and all the righteous: the righteous on the right, the sheep, and the wicked on the left, the goats.

note.label: Life Eternal Or Everlasting Punishment

points: Depart from me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels: the ones on the left, the goats, those that was rebellious towards Christ, that didn't want to listen, are going to be cast into that everlasting fire. This is pain after death.

note.label: Life Eternal Or Everlasting Punishment

points: These shall go away into everlasting punishment: the ones on the left. But the righteous into life eternal.

note.label: Life Eternal Or Everlasting Punishment

points: Emotional avoidance or perfectionism. Let's see what the Lord said to the perfectionist.
Then he which had received the one talent came: so the Lord gave him a talent for him to do something with it. By the time he returned, it needed to be something done with that talent.
Lord, I knew thee that thou art an hard man: so what is he doing? He coming with emotions. I felt like you hard. Like, you all stern. You don't play, Lord.

note.label: Chronic Procrastination

points: And went and hid thy talent in the earth: I ain't want to mess it up. I ain't want to make a mistake. I ain't want to ruin the talent. So I made sure I hid it so that nothing happened to it. That's perfectionism. But it's really emotional avoidance. I was afraid.

note.label: Chronic Procrastination

points: Thou wicked and slothful servant: he don't give a damn about your emotions. Hell no. The Lord don't give a damn about your perfectionism. The hell, you wicked and you slothful.

note.label: Chronic Procrastination

points: Thou oughtest therefore to have put my money to the exchangers: so if you was afraid of how hard I am, for real for real, you would have at least put my money or my talent somewhere where it would have built interest. You won't just let it sit under a rock.

note.label: Chronic Procrastination

points: Take therefore the talent from him: so the talent was taken away from him, and that could be you, if you keep playing with chronic procrastination.

note.label: Chronic Procrastination

points: Five were wise and five were foolish. The foolish took their lamps and took no oil with them; the wise took oil in their vessels with their lamps. The oil is the wisdom of the scriptures.

note.label: Matthew 25: The Ten Virgins, the Talents, and the Sheep and the Goats

points: The foolish come afterward saying, Lord, Lord, open to us, and are answered, Verily I say unto you, I know you not.

note.label: Matthew 25: The Ten Virgins, the Talents, and the Sheep and the Goats

points: Every man received according to his several ability, and the two who traded were told, Well done, thou good and faithful servant.

note.label: Matthew 25: The Ten Virgins, the Talents, and the Sheep and the Goats

points: The one who hid his talent blamed his lord and called him a hard man, and was answered, Thou wicked and slothful servant. That fearful spirit is not of the Most High, and a man should examine himself for it.

note.label: Matthew 25: The Ten Virgins, the Talents, and the Sheep and the Goats

points: Unto every one that hath shall be given, and he shall have abundance; but from him that hath not shall be taken away even that which he hath. Knowledge that is not used is knowledge that is lost.

note.label: Matthew 25: The Ten Virgins, the Talents, and the Sheep and the Goats

points: He separates them one from another, as a shepherd divideth his sheep from the goats, and says to those on the right hand, Inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world.

note.label: Matthew 25: The Ten Virgins, the Talents, and the Sheep and the Goats

points: Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me. Meeting the need of a brother or sister in the body is counted as done to Christ himself.

note.label: Matthew 25: The Ten Virgins, the Talents, and the Sheep and the Goats

points: Those on the left hand are answered with the same measure: inasmuch as ye did it not to one of the least of these, ye did it not to me.

note.label: Matthew 25: The Ten Virgins, the Talents, and the Sheep and the Goats

points: “Then shall the kingdom of heaven be likened unto ten virgins”: that represents Israel. They “took their lamps, and went forth to meet the bridegroom.” Who is the bridegroom? The sun is the bridegroom in Psalms 19.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

points: “And five of them were wise, and five were foolish. They that were foolish took their lamps, and took no oil with them.” The oil is understanding.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

points: “But the wise took oil in their vessels with their lamps.” The oil is the understanding and the lamp is the commandments.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

points: “While the bridegroom tarried”: meaning he was away. Remember, while the light is with you, you are in the light; when the light is gone, where will you be? “They all slumbered and slept.” So they were in darkness.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

points: “And at midnight there was a cry made, Behold, the bridegroom cometh; go ye out to meet him.” That is us going out and teaching our people the word of God: the Lord is returning, repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand. While we slept, now we start waking our people up. Repent, for the kingdom is at hand: that is what John said, what Elijah said.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

points: “Then all those virgins arose, and trimmed their lamps. And the foolish said unto the wise, Give us of your oil; for our lamps are gone out.” They have not done anything; they have not been applying any commandments. “But the wise answered, saying, Not so; lest there be not enough for us and you: but go ye rather to them that sell, and buy for yourselves”: go study.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

points: “And while they went to buy, the bridegroom came; and they that were ready went in with him to the marriage: and the door was shut.” The door was shut to his chamber. They had a wedding.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

points: “Afterward came also the other virgins, saying, Lord, Lord, open to us. But he answered and said, Verily I say unto you, I know you not.”
“Watch therefore, for ye know neither the day nor the hour wherein the Son of man cometh.” The Son of man is the bridegroom: Christ is the bridegroom.
